summary: The full-text HTML version of the proposed rule. The fetch returned it as far as printed page 32212, in the discussion of section 200.206; the raw-text version stopped at page 32210. key_facts: The HTML version was returned to printed page 32212 (discussion of 200.206); the raw-text version to page 32210 (discussion of 200.102).

Preamble, pages 32204-32205: in 200.340 OMB proposes to clarify the text on termination and to give notice of the Government's ability to terminate discretionary awards for discretionary reasons in a manner consistent with law.

Page 32205: the revision would let an agency terminate a discretionary award that is not effective at achieving programme goals or agency priorities, or that the agency otherwise determines is no longer in the Federal Government's interest.
Page 32209 (200.1): the definitions of fixed amount awards and protected personally identifiable information would be removed.

200.204: agencies must publicly announce funding opportunities for all discretionary awards, not only those openly competed; opportunities posted no less than 30 days unless exigent circumstances exist.
200.205: peer review remains advisory; senior appointees must conduct pre-issuance reviews of proposals selected for funding against applicable law, agency priorities and the national interest.
200.206(b)(2): the list of factors an agency may consider in evaluating applicant risk would be expanded.
200.111: announcements, applications and award information must be in English and in U.S. dollars.
quotes: OMB proposes to revise § 200.201(b) to eliminate the use of fixed amount awards unless otherwise authorized by Federal statute.
Proposed revisions in this section also clarify that peer review remains advisory and does not replace agency discretion.
OMB also proposes similar changes related to award suspension.
This proposed change is not intended to impact any existing fixed amount awards or subawards issued prior to the effective date of the proposed rule.

key_facts: Part XI: OMB proposes to issue a final rule that is effective by October 1, 2026, so that a single set of government-wide requirements applies to Federal awards made during fiscal year 2027 (wording as returned on a second read of the same excerpt); OMB gave a 45-day comment period.

Part IX: Executive Order 14332 of August 7, 2025 directed OMB to revise the requirements on indirect cost recovery; fiscal year 2026 appropriations provisions required agencies to keep applying negotiated rates under 200.414 as in fiscal year 2024 and barred specified agencies from using fiscal year 2026 funds to change them.

Part IX: OMB is not proposing updates to the indirect cost rate negotiation system through the document, may consider a request for information later, and tells commenters not to comment on that system.

Preamble on 200.340: OMB proposes to revise 200.340(a) on the reasons for discretionary terminations and to add provisions on temporary suspension, described as similar to procedures for procurement contracts under the FAR.

Preamble on 200.340: under the new discretionary termination provision the agency or pass-through entity, to the extent permitted by law, may terminate an award in part or its entirety if it determines that termination is in its interest, including where the award no longer effectuates programme goals, agency priorities or the national interest as they exist at the time of termination.
Proposed regulatory text, amendatory instruction 87: "Revise § 200.340 to read as follows"; paragraph (a)(1) is headed "For noncompliance by the recipient or subrecipient".

Preamble on 200.342: only minor clarifying revisions; administrative hearing rights continue on a remedy for noncompliance, and such procedures would not be required for other types of terminations unless expressly required by other law.
Preamble on 200.333: OMB proposes to remove the policy allowing recipients to issue fixed amount subawards.
Preamble on 200.421: all advertising and public relations costs unallowable with limited exceptions; the only exception for public relations costs is those required by statute.
Preamble on 200.432: costs of attending conferences allowable only if participation is expressly approved by the agency and included in the terms and conditions of the award.
Preamble on 200.450: three new paragraphs; paragraph (c)(1)(iii) would expressly prohibit funding voter registration campaigns, drives or related activities.
Preamble on 200.454: the only allowable costs are those necessary to fulfil the award requirements, with a new prior approval requirement.
Preamble on 200.461: publication costs unallowable unless expressly required by statute; the word "promotion" removed.
Preamble on 200.300: OMB proposes to streamline references to legal and policy obligations and to supplement the section to reflect administration policies and priorities.
Preamble on new 200.220: prohibits the obligation of Federal funds for covered foreign collaborations; it does not prohibit foreign collaborations using non-Federal funds.

Proposed regulatory text of 200.205: the merit review process, including the pre-issuance review in paragraph (b), must be described or incorporated by reference in the notice of funding opportunity, and the pre-issuance review may form the basis of a decision not to select an applicant.
Preamble on 200.429: the reference to institutions of higher education would be removed so that the restriction applies to all entities.

title: Financial Assistance Regulations-Conflict of Interest and Conflict of Commitment Policy Requirements (final rule), 91 FR 43511
summary: DOE's final rule adding conflict of interest and conflict of commitment requirements to its financial assistance regulations at 2 CFR part 910. It is the amendment that the eCFR banner for title 2 dates 8/17/2026. Read from the Federal Register API record and the raw text.
key_facts: 91 FR 43511; document 2026-14333; published July 16, 2026; final rule; effective August 17, 2026; docket DOE-HQ-2024-0029; RIN 1991-AC18; CFR reference: title 2, part 910.
Applies to any non-Federal entity that is an applicant to or recipient of a DOE financial assistance award on or after August 17, 2026.
Adds subpart C (sections 910.200 to 910.270 and Appendix A) to 2 CFR part 910.
On the effective date subpart C supersedes the interim conflict of interest policy, FAL No. 2022-02.
A covered individual is one who contributes in a substantive, meaningful way to the development or execution of the scope of work of a project.
Conflict of commitment: a situation in which an individual accepts or incurs conflicting obligations, whether foreign or domestic, between or among multiple employers.
910.210(a): non-Federal entities that are applicants to or recipients of a DOE financial assistance award must maintain a written conflict of interest and conflict of commitment policy.
910.230(b): a subrecipient either certifies that its own policy complies or is subject to the recipient's policy.
Programmes of the DOE Office of Indian Energy are excepted.

910.200, significant financial interest: for a publicly traded entity, remuneration plus equity interest exceeding $5,000 in the 12 months before disclosure; for a non-publicly traded entity, remuneration exceeding $5,000 or any equity interest; income from intellectual property; reimbursed or sponsored travel, with exclusions.
910.230(c): covered individuals update disclosures annually and as soon as practicable, but not later than 15 days, after a new conflict arises.
910.230(d): covered individuals complete training before engaging in a DOE-funded project and refresher training at least every two years.
910.240(a): the entity reports to DOE any conflict that cannot be eliminated or managed and any conflict involving a foreign government, its instrumentalities or foreign-controlled entities.

910.260: organisational conflicts are reported within fifteen days of learning of the conflict; the preamble says DOE adopted a 15-day period (re-read 2026-10-05; the first reading returned 15 business days).

No minimum award amount is stated, and the rule gives no waiver for entities that already follow the PHS or NSF policy; DOE declined a one-year lead time and made the rule effective 30 days after publication, August 17, 2026.
Appendix A sets a uniform Disclosure Certification Statement.
quotes: This rule is effective on August 17, 2026.
as soon as practicable, but not later than 15 days
